einzeiler: The rise and violent fall of the notorious Barker-Karpis gang during the Great Depression.
kurzfassung: The Barker-Karpis gang executed a series of high-profile kidnappings and robberies during the Great Depression, culminating in violent clashes with law enforcement. Following major heists like the Edward Bremer kidnapping, the gang members were hunted down, killed in shootouts, or imprisoned in Alcatraz. Ultimately, the gang amassed a massive criminal record that outpaced other infamous outlaws of their era.
stichpunkte: The Barker-Karpis gang hijacked a Swift Meatpacking payroll truck in St. Paul, stealing $33,000 and killing a police guard.
A botched robbery of a Federal Reserve transport truck in downtown Chicago yielded only canceled checks and resulted in the immediate killing of a police officer.
The gang kidnapped Commercial State Bank president Edward Bremer, securing a $200,000 ransom after weeks of tense negotiations.
Following an inside betrayal and mounting pressure from the FBI, Ma Barker and Fred Barker were killed during a massive six-hour shootout with federal agents in Florida.
Doc Barker attempted an escape from Alcatraz in 1939 and was shot and killed by prison guards.
Lloyd Barker served a 25-year sentence at Leavenworth before being killed by his wife shortly after his release.
Alvin Karpis served 33 years behind bars, including 25 years at Alcatraz, before being deported and eventually dying in Spain.
The Barker-Karpis gang stole roughly $3 million, killed 30 people, and were labeled by J. Edgar Hoover as the toughest gang the FBI ever cracked.

clips.hook: A high-risk heist that yielded zero cash
clips.text: The gang discovered that the bags stolen from the Federal Reserve truck contained solely canceled checks rather than actual money.

clips.hook: A massive ransom demand worth millions today
clips.text: The kidnappers targeted a payout of $200,000, an amount comparable to nearly $5 million in modern currency.

clips.hook: A six-hour gun battle with the FBI
clips.text: Fred Barker initiated a massive shootout against federal agents surrounding the cottage, leading to an intense siege involving thousands of rounds.

clips.hook: The longest-running public enemy number one
clips.text: Federal agents intercepted and detained the long-standing fugitive in New Orleans after he held the top spot for eighteen months.

clips.hook: Outpacing every other criminal of the era
clips.text: The criminal organization accumulated more wealth and killed more individuals than famous contemporaries like John Dillinger and Bonnie and Clyde combined.

beschreibung:
In 1934, time runs out for all the high-profile outlaws of the era. The Barker-Karpis Gang commits two more violent robberies – one disastrous – and their most lucrative kidnapping to date, but the FBI is closing in. The gang suffers major losses during a shootout in Florida. One by one, gang members fall until only Alvin Karpis remains. When his time runs out, he becomes one of the celebrity inmates at notorious Alcatraz prison.
